summary: The source permits at most 100 nodes, which is too narrow for honest runtime scaling, while an in-place adjacent-pair swap has a matching linear worst-case lower bound.

optimality.argument: On an even-length list, every one of the L nodes belongs to a pair whose incoming or outgoing link must be inspected and rewired, giving an Omega(L) worst-case lower bound. The iterative implementation advances by two nodes and performs constant work per pair, so its upper bound is O(L).

replacement_checks.evidence: A valid in-place result must reverse every adjacent pair without changing payloads, so no complete pair can be skipped in the worst case.
The current implementation visits each complete pair once, saves its suffix, rewires three boundaries, and carries only fixed pointer state.
Regression checks every legal length from zero through 100 and verifies exact output node identity, order, and unchanged values against both app-local and immutable native sources.
